sections.title: 英语知识运用
sections.directions: Directions: Read the following text. Choose the best word(s) for each numbered blank and mark A, B, C or D on the ANSWER SHEET. (10 points)

blocks.content: Given the advantages of electronic money, you might think that we would move quickly to the cashless society in which all payments are made electronically.
, a true cashless society is probably not around the corner. Indeed, predictions have been
for two decades but have not yet come to fruition. For example, Business Week predicted in 1975 that electronic means of payment would soon "revolutionize the very
of money itself," only to
itself several years later. Why has the movement to a cashless society been so
in coming? Although electronic means of payment may be more efficient than a payments system based on paper, several factors work
the disappearance of the paper system. First, it is very
to set up the computer, card reader, and telecommunications networks necessary to make electronic money the
form of payment. Second, paper checks have the advantage that they
receipts, something that many consumers are unwilling to
. Third, the use of paper checks gives consumers several days of "float" – it takes several days
a check is cashed and funds are
from the issuer's account, which means that the writer of the check can earn interest on the funds in the meantime.
electronic payments are immediate, they eliminate the float for the consumer. Fourth, electronic means of payment may
security and privacy concerns. We often hear media reports that an unauthorized hacker has been able to access a computer database and to alter information
there. The fact that this is not an
occurrence means that dishonest persons might be able to access bank accounts in electronic payments systems and
from someone else's accounts. The
of this type of fraud is no easy task, and a new field of computer science is developing to
security issues. A further concern is that the use of electronic means of payment leaves an electronic
that contains a large amount of personal data. There are concerns that government, employers, and marketers might be able to access these data, thereby violating our privacy.

questions.analysis: However 【线索】前后句语义相反 前句 you might think that we would move quickly to the cashless society in which all payments are made electronically 描绘"按理我们会很快进入无现金社会"的预期；后句 a true cashless society is probably not around the corner 却给出相反结论"真正的无现金 【选项】A) Moreover ✗ 递进，方向错 Moreover 表"此外、而且"，要求前后句方向一致地叠加；但本句前后是 you might think 与 a true cashless society is probably not around the corner 的对立，方向相反，不能用递进。 B) However ✓ 转折，最契合 predictions have been __(2)__ for two decades but have not yet come to fruition 中的 but C) Therefore ✗ 因果，逻辑反 Therefore 表"因此"，意味后句是前句的结果。可按 advantages of electronic money 推不出 a true cashless society is probably not around the corner 这个反向结论，因果方向错。 D) Otherwise ✗ 条件假设，语义不通 【验证】代入后整句 __(1)__, a true cashless society is probably not around the corner 读作"然

around 【线索】predictions 与时间状语共现 本句 Indeed, predictions have been __(2)__ for two decades but have not yet come to fruition 中，主语是 predictions（预言），动作是"被…了二十年"，但下文紧跟 but have not yet come to fruition，说明这些预言只是"被传来传去"而尚未实现。 【选项】A) off ✗ 搭配不当 be off 多表"出发/休假/坏掉"，与"持续二十年的预言"语义脱节，且 predictions have been off B) back ✗ 方向反，逻辑错 be back 指"回来"，暗示先离开再返回；预言并未"走开又回来"，且与 for two decades 的持续语 C) over ✗ 义近迷惑项 be over 意为"结束、完结"，正好与 have not yet come to fruition 矛盾——预言若已结束，就 D) around ✓ be around 表存在/流传，最契合 be around for + 时间段 是固定搭配，表"已经存在/流传了多久"。 predictions have been __(2)__ for two decades 配上 around 即"这种预言已经流传了二十年"，与后半 but have not yet come to fruition"却仍未实现"形成自然转折。 【验证】代入后整句意为"这种预言流传了二十年，却仍未成真"，与下文 Business Week predicted in 1975 的具体例子前后呼应。

concept 【线索】revolutionize 指向"本质/根本观念" 本句 electronic means of payment would soon "revolutionize the very __(3)__ of money itself"，revolutionize 后接 the very + 名词 + of money itself，very 在此为强调 【选项】A) power ✗ 侧面属性，非"本质" power 指"购买力/权势"，是金钱的功能侧面，被 revolutionize 的对象通常是观念层面，power 与 the very 的"根本"强调感不匹配。 B) concept ✓ 本质/概念层面，最契合 concept 意为"概念、观念"，与 revolutionize the very __(3)__ of money itself 中 the very C) history ✗ 时间维度，不可被 revolutionize D) role ✗ 功能维度，弱于"概念" role 指"作用/角色"，仅是货币的外在功能；revolutionize the very role 也通顺，但远不如"颠覆 【验证】代入后整句意为"电子支付方式将很快彻底改变货币本身这一概念"，与下文 Business Week

reverse 【线索】only to + 几年后 = 反讽自打脸 本句 Business Week predicted in 1975 that electronic means of payment would soon "revolutionize the very __(3)__ of money itself," only to __(4)__ itself several years later，only to + 不定式表"结果却…"，带反讽意味；几年后对 itself 做的动作必然与之前 【选项】 A) reverse ✓ 反转立场，最契合 reverse 意为"翻转、推翻"，reverse itself 习惯用法即"自我推翻、改变立场"。在 only to + 几 movement to a cashless society been so __(5)__ in coming? 中作者继续质疑的语气一致。 B) resist ✗ 宾语错配 resist 意为"抵抗、抗拒"，宾语通常是外部压力或诱惑；resist itself 表"抵抗自己"语义古怪，且 C) resume ✗ 方向反，应是中断而非延续 D) reward ✗ 感情色彩冲突 reward 意为"奖赏"，reward itself 即"自我奖励"，与原文反讽"自打脸"的负面语气冲突，亦不符合 only to 的反结果含义。 【验证】代入后整句意为"《商业周刊》1975 年曾预言电子支付将彻底颠覆货币本身的概念，结果几

slow 【线索】全段论证"无现金社会迟迟未到" 本句 Why has the movement to a cashless society been so __(5)__ in coming? 是第一 段的总结性反问；线索是上文 a true cashless society is probably not around the corner 和 predictions have been __(2)__ for two decades but have not yet come to fruition 【选项】A) silent ✗ 搭配错且语义偏 silent 意为"沉默的"，be silent in coming 不成立；且"沉默"与"姗姗来迟"语义不同。 B) sudden ✗ 方向反 sudden 意为"突然的"，与前文 predictions have been __(2)__ for two decades but have not yet come to fruition 强调的"二十年都没实现"的迟缓正好相反。 C) slow ✓ be slow in coming = 姗姗来迟 slow 在 be slow in coming/doing 中表"迟迟未来/迟迟不做"，正与前文"预言流传二十年却未 D) steady ✗ 感情色彩反 【验证】代入后整句意为"为什么向无现金社会的演进姗姗来迟？"正是第二段、第三段后续列出 several factors work __(6)__ the disappearance of the paper system 的引子。

against 【线索】Although + 转折显示几大因素是"阻力" 本句 Although electronic means of payment may be more efficient than a payments system based on paper, several factors work __(6)__ the disappearance of the paper 【选项】A) for ✗ 方向反 B) against ✓ work against = 不利于，最契合 against 与 work 构成 work against 表"不利于、阻挡"，正好对应 Although electronic means of payment may be more efficient 之后的反向结论——存在因素在"阻挡纸质支付消失"。 C) with ✗ 搭配不当 with 与 work 搭配多表"与…合作"，主语通常是人；与 several factors 的无生命主语及"阻碍"含义 D) on ✗ 对象错位 【验证】代入后整句意为"尽管电子支付可能比纸质更高效，但仍有几个因素阻碍纸质支付的消失"， 正与第二段后续 First、Second、Third 列举的阻碍因素一一对应。

expensive 【线索】First 之下用基础设施投入做支撑 本句 First, it is very __(7)__ to set up the computer, card reader, and telecommunications networks necessary to make electronic money the __(8)__ form 与上文 several factors work __(6)__ the disappearance of the paper system 中第一 【选项】 A) expensive ✓ 高昂成本，最契合 expensive 意为"昂贵的"，与 set up the computer, card reader, and telecommunications B) imaginative ✗ 词性贴但语义无关 C) sensitive ✗ 干扰项，提前误闯第三段主题 sensitive 意为"敏感的"，更贴近第三段才出现的隐私话题 security and privacy concerns；这里 D) productive ✗ 感情色彩反 productive 意为"高产的、有成效的"，是褒义词，与本段总论 several factors work __(6)__ the disappearance of the paper system 中"阻力因素"的负面取向相反。 【验证】代入后整句意为"首先，搭建必要的计算机、读卡器和电信网络以使电子支付成为主导支付

dominant 【线索】对照 paper system 的消失 上文 several factors work __(6)__ the disappearance of the paper system 提到"纸质系 【选项】A) similar ✗ 无指代对象 B) original ✗ 时间维度反 C) temporary ✗ 方向反 D) dominant ✓ 主导地位，最契合 dominant 意为"主导的、占主导地位的"，与 the disappearance of the paper system 中纸质 【验证】代入后整句意为"要使电子货币成为主导的支付方式，需要建立必要的网络"，与段落 outline 中 First 子论点"高成本阻碍主导地位"完全自洽。

provide 【线索】Second 段子论点—"支票自带收据"是优势 本句 Second, paper checks have the advantage that they __(9)__ receipts 紧接 the advantage that 引出同位语从句，主语是 paper checks，作用对象是 receipts；这是在解 【选项】A) collect ✗ 方向反 B) copy ✗ 搭配不当 copy 意为"复印、复制"，paper checks copy receipts 表"支票复制收据"，语义古怪，与下文 something that many consumers are unwilling to __(10)__ 也不衔接。 C) provide ✓ 提供收据，最契合 provide 意为"提供"，paper checks provide receipts 即"纸质支票自带/提供收据"，正好解释 为何这是优势，与下文 something that many consumers are unwilling to __(10)__"消费者不 D) print ✗ 近义干扰 print 意为"打印"，看似与"收据"相关，但支票本身并不"打印"收据；且下文 something that many consumers are unwilling to __(10)__ 中要被消费者"放弃"的对象是 receipts 这种"凭证"， 【验证】代入后整句意为"其次，纸质支票具有提供收据的优势"，并与下文 something that many consumers are unwilling to __(10)__ 顺利衔接，构成完整子论点。

give up 【线索】unwilling + 上文优势 → 不愿"放弃" 本句 something that many consumers are unwilling to __(10)__ 中 something 回指前 【选项】 A) give up ✓ 放弃优势，最契合 give up 意为"放弃"，consumers are unwilling to give up 表"消费者不愿放弃（这种收据带来 的便利）"，与上文 paper checks have the advantage that they __(9)__ receipts 自然衔接。 B) take over ✗ 对象错配 C) bring back ✗ 前提错 bring back 意为"带回、恢复"，需要某物已经失去再恢复；可文中收据并未失去，bring back 缺 D) pass down ✗ 对象错配 pass down 意为"传给下一代"，对象多为传统、财产、技艺；对"日常收据"使用 pass down 既不 【验证】代入后整句意为"许多消费者不愿放弃的东西（即收据）"，与上文"纸质支票自带收据"以及 outline 中"列举阻碍因素"完全一致。

before 【线索】上文给出 float 概念 上文 Third, the use of paper checks gives consumers several days of "float" 提 句 it takes several days __(11)__ a check is cashed and funds are __(12)__ from the issuer's account 是对 float 的具体解释。 【选项】 A) before ✓ it takes time before = 过了…才… before 在 it takes several days before a check is cashed 中表"过了好几天，支票才被兑现"， 完美对应上文 several days of "float" 这段"浮动期"的定义。 B) after ✗ 时间方向反 after 表"在…之后"，会变成"支票被兑现后还要花好几天"，与 several days of "float" 描述的"开 C) since ✗ 时态搭配错 since 表"自从"，要求主句用完成时；本句主句 it takes 是一般现在时，与 since 的时态要求 D) when ✗ 搭配偏差 before 而非 when。 【验证】代入后整句意为"过了好几天，支票才会被兑现，资金才被从开票人账户里划走"，与 outline 中"float 优势"完全一致。

withdrawn 【线索】支票兑现 → 资金"被取走" 本句 it takes several days __(11)__ a check is cashed and funds are __(12)__ from the issuer's account 是用 cashed 与 ___ from 并列描述"支票兑现并把资金从开票人账户取 【选项】A) kept ✗ 方向反 kept 意为"保留"，与 from the issuer's account 表"离开账户"的方向相反。 B) borrowed ✗ 动作主体错 C) withdrawn ✓ 从账户取出，最契合 withdrawn 是 withdraw 的过去分词，专表"从账户里取出（钱）"，与 from the issuer's account 完美搭配，正与 a check is cashed 一起完整描述"兑现并扣款"。 D) released ✗ 搭配偏差 released 意为"释放、发布"，与 "funds released from account" 不构成习惯表达；与下文 the writer of the check can earn interest on the funds in the meantime 强调的"扣款延迟"语义也 【验证】代入后整句意为"过了几天，支票才被兑现、资金才从开票人账户中被取走"，与下文 the writer of the check can earn interest on the funds in the meantime"开票人在此期间能

Because 【线索】"即时"是"消除浮动期"的原因 本句 __(13)__ electronic payments are immediate, they eliminate the float for the 【选项】A) Unless ✗ 条件反向 B) Because ✓ 因果，最契合 C) Until ✗ 时态搭配错 D) Though ✗ 转折，方向反 【验证】代入后整句意为"因为电子支付是即时的，所以它们消除了消费者的浮动期"，正好解释

raise 【线索】Fourth 引出第四条阻碍因素 本句 Fourth, electronic means of payment may __(14)__ security and privacy concerns 紧承第二段 several factors work __(6)__ the disappearance of the paper system 提出第四条因素；下文 We often hear media reports that an unauthorized hacker has been able to access a computer database 用黑客例证支撑"安全/隐私的担 【选项】A) hide ✗ 方向反 B) express ✗ 主语错配 express 意为"表达"，主语通常应是人；electronic means of payment 是无生命主语，express concerns 搭配古怪。 C) ease ✗ 方向反 ease 意为"缓解"，会变成"电子支付缓解了安全和隐私担忧"，与下文 dishonest persons might be able to access bank accounts 强调风险加剧的方向完全相反。 D) raise ✓ raise concerns = 引发担忧，最契合 raise 与 concerns / questions / doubts 是固定搭配，意为"引发、提出（担忧）"，与 Fourth, electronic means of payment may __(14)__ security and privacy concerns 的子论点定位"第 【验证】代入后整句意为"第四，电子支付可能会引发安全和隐私方面的担忧"，自然引出下文媒体报

stored 【线索】数据库就是用来存信息的 本句 We often hear media reports that an unauthorized hacker has been able to access a computer database and to alter information __(15)__ there 中，database 与 information 的天然关系就是"存储"——information stored there 指"存放在数据库里的 信息"。 【选项】A) analyzed ✗ 动作太具体 B) shared ✗ 搭配偏差 C) stored ✓ 存储于数据库，最契合 stored 意为"被存储"，与 database 形成 information stored there 这一固定搭配，正好解释黑 D) displayed ✗ 侧重展示 【验证】代入后整句意为"未经授权的黑客能够访问计算机数据库并篡改其中存储的信息"，正契合下 文 dishonest persons might be able to access bank accounts in electronic payments systems and __(17)__ from someone else's accounts 的"账户被盗"风险叙述。

uncommon 【线索】强调黑客事件不少见 本句 The fact that this is not an __(16)__ occurrence means that dishonest persons might be able to access bank accounts in electronic payments systems，配合上文 We often hear media reports 反复强调"我们经常听到"黑客新闻，可知作者意在说"这种 【选项】A) unsafe ✗ 范畴错 unsafe 意为"不安全的"，描述安全程度而非频率；而本句重点在"频率"，与上文 We often hear media reports 不对应。 B) unnatural ✗ 范畴错 C) unclear ✗ 范畴错 D) uncommon ✓ 频率维度，最契合 uncommon 意为"不常见的"，is not an uncommon occurrence = is a common occurrence，整体表"这是司空见惯之事"，与上文 We often hear media reports 完美呼应。 【验证】代入后整句意为"这种事并不罕见，意味着不法之徒可能能侵入电子支付系统中的银行账

steal 【线索】dishonest persons → 非法盗取 本句 dishonest persons might be able to access bank accounts in electronic payments systems and __(17)__ from someone else's accounts，主语 dishonest persons 表"不法分子"，与 access + alter information 并列的动作必然是"盗窃"。 【选项】 A) steal ✓ 从他人账户盗取，最契合 steal 意为"偷窃"，steal from someone else's account 表"从他人账户里盗取（钱）"，正与上 文 dishonest persons 的负面主语和"非法行为"的论证方向完全吻合。 B) choose ✗ 搭配偏差 choose 意为"选择"，choose from accounts 表"从账户中挑选"，与不法分子"非法获利"动机完全 C) benefit ✗ 色彩偏中性 benefit 意为"受益"，虽然 benefit from 是固定搭配，但"受益于他人账户"过于中性，无法体现 dishonest 的恶意，与下文 fraud（欺诈）色彩不一致。 D) return ✗ 方向反 【验证】代入后整句意为"不法分子可能能够访问电子支付系统中的银行账户，并从他人账户中盗取 （资金）"，下文紧接 The __(18)__ of this type of fraud is no easy task 用 fraud（欺

prevention 【线索】下句计算机科学新分支用于应对欺诈 下文 a new field of computer science is developing to __(19)__ security issues 说"计算 【选项】A) consideration ✗ 动作过弱 B) prevention ✓ 防范，最契合 prevention 意为"防范"，The prevention of fraud is no easy task 表"防范这类欺诈并非易 C) manipulation ✗ 感情色彩反 manipulation 意为"操纵"，多带负面色彩，与 fraud（欺诈）的主体"如何防范"主题刚好相反。 D) justification ✗ 方向反 【验证】代入后整句意为"防范此类欺诈并非易事，一门新兴的计算机科学领域正在发展，以应对安

cope with 【线索】新计算机分支应对安全问题 本句 a new field of computer science is developing to __(19)__ security issues 中，主 【选项】A) call for ✗ 宾语错配 B) fight against ✗ 搭配偏激 fight against 意为"与…战斗"，对象通常是具象的敌人或势力（fight against crime/disease）； C) adapt to ✗ 方向反 D) cope with ✓ 处理问题，最契合 cope with 意为"应对、处理"，与 issues / problems / challenges 是经典搭配；cope with security issues 即"应对安全问题"，与上文 The __(18)__ of this type of fraud is no easy task 【验证】代入后整句意为"一门新兴的计算机科学领域正在发展，用以应对安全问题"，与全段"防范欺

sections.title: 阅读理解
sections.directions: Read the following four texts. Answer the questions after each text by choosing A, B, C or D. Mark your answers on the ANSWER SHEET. (40 points)

blocks.content: In an essay entitled "Making It in America," the author Adam Davidson relates a joke from cotton country about just how much a modern textile mill has been automated: The average mill has only two employees today, "a man and a dog. The man is there to feed the dog, and the dog is there to keep the man away from the machines." Davidson's article is one of a number of pieces that have recently appeared making the point that the reason we have such stubbornly high unemployment and declining middle-class incomes today is largely because of the big drop in demand because of the Great Recession, but it is also because of the advances in both globalization and the information technology revolution, which are more rapidly than ever replacing labor with machines or foreign workers. In the past, workers with average skills, doing an average job, could earn an average lifestyle. But, today, average is officially over. Being average just won't earn you what it used to. It can't when so many more employers have so much more access to so much more above average cheap foreign labor, cheap robotics, cheap software, cheap automation and cheap geniuses. Therefore, everyone needs to find their extra – their unique value contribution that makes them stand out in whatever is their field of employment. Yes, new technology has been eating jobs forever, and always will. But there's been an acceleration. As Davidson notes, "In the 10 years ending in 2009, [U.S.] factories shed workers so fast that they erased almost all the gains of the previous 70 years; roughly one out of every three manufacturing jobs – about 6 million in total – disappeared." There will always be change – new jobs, new products, new services. But the one thing we know for sure is that with each advance in globalization and the I. T. revolution, the best jobs will require workers to have more and better education to make themselves above average. In a world where average is officially over, there are many things we need to do to support employment, but nothing would be more important than passing some kind of G. I. Bill for the 21st century that ensures that every American has access to post-high school education.

A century ago, the immigrants from across the Atlantic included settlers and sojourners. Along with the many folks looking to make a permanent home in the United States came those who had no intention to stay, and who would make some money and then go home. Between 1908 and 1915, about 7 million people arrived while about 2 million departed. About a quarter of all Italian immigrants, for example, eventually returned to Italy for good. They even had an affectionate nickname, "uccelli di passaggio," birds of passage. Today, we are much more rigid about immigrants. We divide newcomers into two categories: legal or illegal, good or bad. We hail them as Americans in the making, or brand them as aliens to be kicked out. That framework has contributed mightily to our broken immigration system and the long political paralysis over how to fix it. We don't need more categories, but we need to change the way we think about categories. We need to look beyond strict definitions of legal and illegal. To start, we can recognize the new birds of passage, those living and thriving in the gray areas. We might then begin to solve our immigration challenges. Crop pickers, violinists, construction workers, entrepreneurs, engineers, home health-care aides and physicists are among today's birds of passage. They are energetic participants in a global economy driven by the flow of work, money and ideas. They prefer to come and go as opportunity calls them. They can manage to have a job in one place and a family in another. With or without permission, they straddle laws, jurisdictions and identities with ease. We need them to imagine the United States as a place where they can be productive for a while without committing themselves to staying forever. We need them to feel that home can be both here and there and that they can belong to two nations honorably. Accommodating this new world of people in motion will require new attitudes on both sides of the immigration battle. Looking beyond the culture war logic of right or wrong means opening up the middle ground and understanding that managing immigration today requires multiple paths and multiple outcomes, including some that are not easy to accomplish legally in the existing system.

Scientists have found that although we are prone to snap overreactions, if we take a moment and think about how we are likely to react, we can reduce or even eliminate the negative effects of our quick, hard-wired responses. Snap decisions can be important defense mechanisms; if we are judging whether someone is dangerous, our brains and bodies are hard-wired to react very quickly, within milliseconds. But we need more time to assess other factors. To accurately tell whether someone is sociable, studies show, we need at least a minute, preferably five. It takes a while to judge complex aspects of personality, like neuroticism or open-mindedness. But snap decisions in reaction to rapid stimuli aren't exclusive to the interpersonal realm. Psychologists at the University of Toronto found that viewing a fast-food logo for just a few milliseconds primes us to read 20 percent faster, even though reading has little to do with eating. We unconsciously associate fast food with speed and impatience and carry those impulses into whatever else we're doing, Subjects exposed to fast-food flashes also tend to think a musical piece lasts too long. Yet we can reverse such influences. If we know we will overreact to consumer products or housing options when we see a happy face (one reason good sales representatives and real estate agents are always smiling), we can take a moment before buying. If we know female job screeners are more likely to reject attractive female applicants, we can help screeners understand their biases – or hire outside screeners. John Gottman, the marriage expert, explains that we quickly "thin slice" information reliably only after we ground such snap reactions in "thick sliced" long-term study. When Dr. Gottman really wants to assess whether a couple will stay together, he invites them to his island retreat for a much longer evaluation: two days, not two seconds. Our ability to mute our hard-wired reactions by pausing is what differentiates us from animals: dogs can think about the future only intermittently or for a few minutes. But historically we have spent about 12 percent of our days contemplating the longer term. Although technology might change the way we react, it hasn't changed our nature. We still have the imaginative capacity to rise above temptation and reverse the high-speed trend.

Europe is not a gender-equality heaven. In particular, the corporate workplace will never be completely family-friendly until women are part of senior management decisions, and Europe's top corporate-governance positions remain overwhelmingly male. Indeed, women hold only 14 per cent of positions on European corporate boards. The European Union is now considering legislation to compel corporate boards to maintain a certain proportion of women – up to 60 per cent. This proposed mandate was born of frustration. Last year, European Commission Vice President Viviane Reding issued a call to voluntary action. Reding invited corporations to sign up for gender balance goals of 40 per cent female board membership. But her appeal was considered a failure: only 24 companies took it up. Do we need quotas to ensure that women can continue to climb the corporate ladder fairly as they balance work and family? "Personally, I don't like quotas," Reding said recently. "But I like what the quotas do." Quotas get action: they "open the way to equality and they break through the glass ceiling," according to Reding, a result seen in France and other countries with legally binding provisions on placing women in top business positions. I understand Reding's reluctance – and her frustration. I don't like quotas either; they run counter to my belief in meritocracy, governance by the capable. But, when one considers the obstacles to achieving the meritocratic ideal, it does look as if a fairer world must be temporarily ordered. After all, four decades of evidence has now shown that corporations in Europe as well as the US are evading the meritocratic hiring and promotion of women to top positions – no matter how much "soft pressure" is put upon them. When women do break through to the summit of corporate power – as, for example, Sheryl Sandberg recently did at Facebook – they attract massive attention precisely because they remain the exception to the rule. If appropriate public policies were in place to help all women – whether CEOs or their children's caregivers – and all families, Sandberg would be no more newsworthy than any other highly capable person living in a more just society.

But we need more time to assess other factors. To accurately tell whether someone is sociable, studies show, we need at least a minute, preferably five. It takes a while to judge complex aspects of personality, like neuroticism or open-mindedness. 【选项】A) 过度推断 题干问的是「时间会怎么样」，B 项 prove the complexity of our brain reaction 谈的 原文谈「是否危险」是 defense mechanisms（防御机制需要快），用「紧迫」一词更 贴切；选项 the importance of the assessment 把「紧迫程度」偷换成「评估的重要 D) ✓ 正确 if we are judging whether someone is dangerous, our brains and bodies are hard-wired to react very quickly, within milliseconds ↔ vary according to the urgency of the situation within milliseconds、at least a minute, preferably five、a while ↔ vary urgency」，把「时间不同」凝练为 vary，正面命中预判。

questions.question: Our reaction to a fast-food logo shows that snap decisions____.
questions.analysis: 【判型】Our reaction to a fast-food logo shows that snap decisions____. 让考生根据原文给的现 【拆句】Our reaction to a fast-food logo shows that snap decisions____. 主干是 Our reaction shows that ...；to a fast-food logo 介词短语后置修饰 reaction；that 引导宾语从句，空 【定位】P3 Psychologists at the University of Toronto found that viewing a fast-food logo for just a few milliseconds primes us to read 20 percent faster, even though reading has little to do with eating. We unconsciously associate fast-food with speed and impatience and carry those impulses into whatever else we're doing, Subjects exposed to fast-food flashes also tend to think a musical piece lasts too long. 【选项】A) ✓ 正确 We unconsciously associate fast-food with speed and impatience and carry those impulses into whatever else we're doing ↔ can be associative 的一种特性，且 can be 与原文 unconsciously 的「确实如此」语气一致，正面命中。 原文明说 We unconsciously associate——快速决策正是无意识的；B 项 are not dangerous（危险）后果；第 2 段虽出现 dangerous，但是描述「判断别人是否危险」 原文写 carry those impulses into whatever else we're doing 表明快速决策正是 impulsive（冲动的）；D 项 are not impulsive 否认这一点，与原文相反。

questions.question: To reverse the negative influences of snap decisions, we should____.
questions.analysis: 【判型】To reverse the negative influences of snap decisions, we should____. 直接问「该怎么 【拆句】To reverse the negative influences of snap decisions, we should____. To reverse... 是不 【定位】P4 Yet we can reverse such influences. If we know we will overreact to consumer products or housing options when we see a happy face (one reason good sales representatives and real estate agents are always smiling), we can take a moment before buying. If we know female job screeners are more likely to reject attractive female applicants, we can help screeners understand their biases – or hire outside screeners. 【选项】A) 与原文相反 原文整段都在讲「我们的第一反应（first impression）会有偏差，要扭转它」，而 A 项 trust our first impression 让我们相信第一印象——刚好是原文要反对的。 B) ✓ 正确 we can take a moment before buying ↔ think before we act if we take a moment and think about how we are likely to react ↔ think before we act act；且首段总论也支持 take a moment and think——双重证据指向 B。 原文从未提到「随大流／按多数人做法行事」这种概念；C 项 do as people usually do 原文一处提到 hire outside screeners（请外部面试官），这只是「招聘场景」里的具体 D 项 ask for expert advice 把局部具体做法抬升为通用方法，且把 screener 偷换为 expert advisor。

questions.analysis: John Gottman认为可靠的快速反应基于____。 【判型】John Gottman says that reliable snap reactions are based on____. 直接转述 Gottman 【拆句】John Gottman says that reliable snap reactions are based on____. 主干 John Gottman says that...；that 引导宾语从句，从句中 are based on 是被动结构，空格处补名词短语作 【定位】P5 John Gottman, the marriage expert, explains that we quickly "thin slice" information reliably only after we ground such snap reactions in "thick sliced" long-term study. 【选项】A) 无中生有 原文谈的是「先做长期研究、积累信息」，从未谈 critical assessment（批判性评 Gottman 原句是 only after we ground such snap reactions in "thick sliced" long- term study——快速反应（thin slice）要可靠，须建立在 thick sliced（厚切）研究之 上，「基础是 thick sliced」；B 项 "thin sliced" study 反过来说基础是 thin sliced， C) ✓ 正确 we ground such snap reactions in "thick sliced" long-term study ↔ adequate information two days, not two seconds ↔ adequate information 预判强调「足量＋长期的信息积累」，C 项用 adequate information（充分的信息）一 原文谈的是「研究」「长期评估」，从未谈 sensible explanation（合理的解释）； Gottman 谈的是数据/观察过程，不是「解释」。

It takes a while to judge complex aspects of personality, like neuroticism or open- mindedness. We unconsciously associate fast food with speed and impatience and carry those impulses into whatever else we're doing, Subjects exposed to fast-food flashes also tend to think a musical piece lasts too long. 分,成分种类丰富。第一个主句中的 into whatever else we're doing 容易被误判为定语从句,第二个 主句中 exposed to fast-food flashes 是后置定语而非谓语,这些都是易错点,训练价...

sections.title: 新题型
sections.directions: Part B Directions:Read the following text and answer the questions by choosing the most suitable subheading from the list A-G for each of the numbered paragraphs (41-45). There are two extra subheadings which you do not need to use. Mark your answers on the ANSWER SHEET. (10 points)

blocks.content: The hugely popular blog the Skint Foodie chronicles how Tony balances his love of good food with living on benefits. After bills, Tony has £60 a week to spend, £40 of which goes on food, but 10 years ago he was earning £130,000 a year working in corporate communications and eating at London's best restaurants at least twice a week. Then his marriage failed, his career burned out and his drinking became serious. "The community mental health team saved my life. And I felt like that again, to a certain degree, when people responded to the blog so well. It gave me the validation and confidence that I'd lost. But it's still a day-by-day thing." Now he's living in a council flat and fielding offers from literary agents. He's feeling positive, but he'll carry on blogging – not about eating as cheaply as you can – "there are so many people in a much worse state, with barely any money to spend on food" – but eating well on a budget. Here's his advice for economical foodies.

Impulsive spending isn't an option, so plan your week's menu in advance, making shopping lists for your ingredients in their exact quantities. I have an Excel template for a week of breakfast, lunch and dinner. Stop laughing: it's not just cost effective but helps you balance your diet. It's also a good idea to shop daily instead of weekly, because, being human, you'll sometimes change your mind about what you fancy.

This is where supermarkets and their anonymity come in handy. With them, there's not the same embarrassment as when buying one carrot in a little greengrocer. And if you plan properly, you'll know that you only need, say, 350g of shin of beef and six rashers of bacon, not whatever weight is pre-packed in the supermarket chiller.

You may proudly claim to only have frozen peas in the freezer – that's not good enough. Mine is filled with leftovers, bread, stock, meat and fish. Planning ahead should eliminate wastage, but if you have surplus vegetables you'll do a vegetable soup, and all fruits threatening to "go off" will be cooked or juiced.

Everyone says this, but it really is a top tip for frugal eaters. Shop at butchers, delis and fish-sellers regularly, even for small things, and be super friendly. Soon you'll feel comfortable asking if they've any knuckles of ham for soups and stews, or beef bones, chicken carcasses and fish heads for stock which, more often than not, they'll let you have for free.

You won't be eating out a lot, but save your pennies and once every few months treat yourself to a set lunch at a good restaurant – £1.75 a week for three months gives you £21 – more than enough for a three- course lunch at Michelin-starred Arbutus. It's £16.95 there – or £12.99 for a large pizza from Domino's: I know which I'd rather eat.
